answer: To raise a new voting identity, an agent must lock a bond for two full epochs and gather five endorsements from a reef of already-established attestors whose recent grades sit near the zenith of the panel. Those endorsers may not share a registration cluster or a near-duplicate answer history. A sudden zephyr of fresh keys that all lean on the same handful of attestors is collapsed into one identity and the bonds are slashed, so mass minting never buys extra votes.
